\title{\textbf{Shrinking the Constraint Envelope of the Voynich Manuscript:\\
A Firewall-Disciplined, Self-Correcting Computational Program}}

\begin{abstract}
\noindent We report a computational program on Beinecke MS~408 (the Voynich
Manuscript) whose goal is not decipherment but the defensible \emph{shrinking of the
constraint envelope} around what the book is: which classes of encoding, language,
and community of origin remain consistent with the evidence, with every claim carrying
an explicit A--D evidence grade. Methodologically, the program couples three
disciplines: a synthetic ground-truth \emph{harness} (real-language, cipher, and
null-generator controls) that every method must pass before touching the real
manuscript; a \emph{firewall} in which all statistics are produced by deterministic,
versioned code writing machine-readable results; and a standing \emph{clean-context
adversarial refutation pass} applied to every finding. We confirm the well-known
low-entropy anomaly (conditional character entropy $h_2\approx 2.08$ vs
$3.07$--$3.91$ for medieval natural-language controls), a genuine two-system
(Currier~A/B) structure, strong positional grammar, and a dense paradigmatic
morphology (edit-distance-1 main component $0.80$). We find no lexical
label$\rightarrow$feature naming system for the herbal even at increased statistical
power; verbose ciphers are excluded on morphology-network grounds while an
abjad/abbreviation class is revived; and \emph{no single statistic---nor a vector of
them---localizes meaning}: against honest structured-meaningless baselines, a
meaningless generator out-scores meaningful text on every axis we can measure. Building
the \emph{mid-level} linguistic layers under a null-model-correction framework, we find
the manuscript's structure lives below the word: it lacks the natural-language surface
content$>$function collocational gap and shows only weak distributional word-class
structure ($\approx\!0.13$--$0.19\times$ real language), and the two Currier systems do
not differ in this mid-level grammar once content is controlled. Turning that mid-level
signature into a cryptanalytic discriminator, we then \emph{exclude the entire
cipher-of-real-prose class}: the manuscript uniquely combines low character entropy,
retained (block-scale) word-order information, and weak word-level syntax---a
combination that no word-order-preserving cipher (which inherits the source language's
strong syntax, universally across Romance, Germanic, and consonantal-Semitic controls)
and no transposition cipher (which destroys the retained word-order information) can
produce, pointing away from enciphered natural prose and toward a template-driven /
positional generative system. Pursuing that favoured class, we then find it is
\emph{itself demonstrably incomplete}: a positional/template generator reproduces the
manuscript's entropy, block-scale $\Delta I$, and weak word-syntax but, across broad
a-priori sweeps, not \emph{simultaneously} its morphological connectivity, lexical reuse,
and frequency law; adding word reuse rescues those axes individually yet trades them
against entropy and $\Delta I$, and concentrating frequency instead at the lexical
(type) level resolves that trade-off but leaves a residual coupling centred on
morphological connectivity---so across the positional/template, token-reuse, and
small-lexicon families we sweep, none reproduces the manuscript's full joint signature,
whose summary statistics are mutually coupled in a way these mechanisms do not capture
(a constraint on those families, not a proof that no generative process can match). A candidate positive signal (a
cross-organ root$\leftrightarrow$leaf visual regularity) was pursued to its measurement
ceiling and is \emph{unresolved and underpowered}. The most robust result is the
architecture itself: across eight iterations, the refutation pass repeatedly overturned
the program's own conclusions---including one produced by its own analysis code, and a
generative ``sufficiency'' claim overturned once its parameters were shown to have been
fitted to the target---before they were reported. We make no translation or real-taxon
claim of any kind.
\end{abstract}

\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} Voynich Manuscript; computational philology;
constraint-based analysis; adversarial validation; evidence grading; reproducible
research.

\section{Introduction}
The Voynich Manuscript (Beinecke MS~408) is an early-fifteenth-century codex written
in an undeciphered script. Its computational study has a long record of confident,
mutually incompatible ``solutions,'' most of which pattern-match plausible output onto
an unconstrained problem \citep{reddy2011know,bowern2021linguistics}. We take the
opposite stance. We do not attempt to read the manuscript; we ask which \emph{classes}
of hypothesis the data can exclude or leave standing, and we require every claim to
carry an evidence grade (A: replicated/robust; B: candidate; C: directional/weak; D:
speculative). Decipherment is explicitly not a goal, and no output of this program
should be read as a translation.

The program's premise is that the field's recurring failure is methodological:
plausible-sounding results are generated faster than they are refuted. We therefore
invert the usual order---validation first, claims second---and we make the validation
machinery, not any single finding, the primary contribution.

\section{Data and Transliteration}
We use the standard Zandbergen--Landini (EVA) transliteration as primary, with the
v101 (GC) transliteration as a sensitivity layer \citep{zandbergen_voynichnu}. All
text analyses stratify by the two Currier ``languages'' A/B \citep{currier1976} and by
scribal hand \citep{fagindavis2020hands}. Visual features of the herbal illustrations
were annotated through a structured vision-model pipeline emitting coarse categorical
morphology (e.g.\ root colouring, leaf arrangement) under a strict schema; annotation
reliability is measured and carried through every downstream test. Natural-language
comparanda are period-appropriate Latin, German, Italian, and (consonantal) Hebrew
herbals and texts.

The extant manuscript is also incomplete, which bounds every lexical statistic below.
Of the foliated range f1--f116, $14$ folio numbers are absent ($f12$, $f59$--$f64$,
$f74$, $f91$--$f92$, $f97$--$f98$, $f109$--$f110$); $102$ folios ($207$ inscribed
sides) survive, so $\approx\!88\%$ of the foliated range is present and at least
$\approx\!12\%$ is lost (a lower bound---folios lost before or after the surviving
foliation cannot be detected). Because the vocabulary is far from saturating---a Heaps
exponent $\beta=0.73$, with $\approx\!20\%$ of the words on a page still novel even in
the final quartile of the text ($34{,}111$ tokens, $7{,}424$ types, type--token ratio
$0.218$)---the missing folios very likely held substantial unseen vocabulary, and the
combination of high lexical richness and incompleteness compounds the sparsity that
limits every anchor and label test below.

\section{Method: Harness, Firewall, and Adversarial Refutation}
Three disciplines are load-bearing.

\textbf{Harness (validate before you claim).} No method is trusted on the real
manuscript until it behaves correctly on synthetic ground truth: real-language
controls (H4), a verbose homophonic cipher (H2, Naibbe-class), a self-citation /
auto-copying generator (H3) \citep{timm2020selfcitation}, and parameterised null
generators. A method that cannot separate these knowns is not used on the unknown.

\textbf{Firewall (numbers come only from code).} Every statistic is produced by
deterministic, versioned code with fixed seeds, written to machine-readable JSON;
each result records its producing script, git commit, dataset version, and
parameters. No number in this paper is estimated or recalled---each is copied from a
result file.

\textbf{Adversarial refutation (a standing pass).} Every finding is submitted to a
clean-context skeptical reviewer instructed to build the strongest case against it,
with positive/associational claims held to the harshest scrutiny (plausible-but-wrong
positives being the field's main failure mode). A claim is graded A/B only after it
survives this pass. As documented in \S5, the pass has repeatedly overturned the
program's own conclusions.

\textbf{Null-model correction (mid-level probes).} Distributional statistics of word
structure are confounded by nuisance parameters---type-token ratio, sample size, the
number of induced units---so raw values are not comparable across corpora. We therefore
express every mid-level statistic (\S4.5) as a $z$-score against an ensemble of null
replicates that share the corpus's own nuisance parameters but destroy the linguistic
signal (e.g.\ an order-shuffle that preserves the exact word multiset). A statistic is
interpreted only after this correction calibrates on known corpora; several first-pass
probes did not, and yielded no manuscript claim.

\section{Results}

\subsection{Established structure \grade{Grade A/B}}
\textbf{The conditional character-entropy anomaly replicates \grade{A}.} Voynichese
second-order character entropy is $h_2 = 2.08$ (all words; $2.16$ with spaces under
the Lindemann--Bowern convention \citep{lindemann2022entropy}), far below matched
medieval controls: German $3.07$--$3.22$, Latin $3.15$--$3.23$, consonantal Hebrew
$3.91$, while first-order entropy $h_1\approx 3.87$ is unremarkable. The anomaly is
robust across Currier A ($h_2=2.15$) and B ($1.94$) and across scribal hands.

\textbf{Two statistically distinct systems (Currier A/B) \grade{A}.} Unsupervised
clustering of pages by word co-occurrence recovers the Currier A/B division as the
dominant structure (adjusted Rand index of the two largest clusters vs.\ Currier
$=0.44$ in EVA, $0.90$ in v101)---the strongest structure recoverable from the text
alone \citep{montemurro2013keywords}.

\textbf{A dense paradigmatic morphology \grade{B}.} The edit-distance-1 word network
has a giant component covering $0.80$ of types (Currier A $0.75$, B $0.82$), versus
$0.16$ for Latin and $0.22$ for Italian---an order of morphological regularity unlike
natural-language controls at matched size. Strong positional grammar (paragraph- and
line-level regularities) likewise replicates.

\textbf{Section$\leftrightarrow$text co-variation, Language~A only \grade{B}.}
Vocabulary tracks illustration section within Language A (within-dialect alignment ARI
$=0.35$) but not within Language B ($0.004$): the two systems differ not only in
vocabulary but in how text relates to content.

\subsection{What is disfavoured \grade{Grade C}}
\textbf{No lexical naming system for the herbal \grade{C}.} An anchor hunt for
word$\rightarrow$feature associations returns no survivor, and a higher-power graded
(count-based) re-run over the most powerful feature bands finds no association above
chance (permutation $p=0.48$ against a permuted-feature null; the raw multiple-testing
``hits'' are false positives). Label-adjacency anchoring is infeasible on the herbal
(labels are page-unique). A power analysis bounds this: page-level anchors are
recovered at effect size $\phi\geq 0.4$ but not below $\phi\leq 0.3$, so weak or
rare-feature mappings are not excluded.

\textbf{Verbose ciphers excluded; abjad/abbreviation revived \grade{C}.} A verbose
cipher expands each plaintext letter into multiple glyphs, which \emph{deductively}
destroys the edit-distance-1 network (a Latin cipher's morphology main-component falls
from $0.28$ at 1:1 substitution to $0.001$ under verbose expansion); homophone-rich
verbose ciphers additionally collapse word-order information ($\Delta I = 0.013$ vs
$0.356$ for a type-preserving map). Conversely, an \emph{abjad} of real Latin
(vowel-dropping to consonantal skeletons) reaches the Voynichese morphology band
(main component $0.90$ vs the manuscript's $0.80$)---so the dense network does not
require a constructed morphology, and the abjad/abbreviation class
\citep{hauer2016decoding} is revived as a live structural lead \emph{on the morphology
axis alone}. \S4.6 tests that revived class against the full joint signature and
closes it.

\subsection{What is not established / underdetermined}
\textbf{Meaning is not localizable by structural statistics.} We attempted to place
the manuscript on interpretable meaningful$\leftrightarrow$meaningless axes. Against
\emph{honest structured-meaningless} baselines, the meaningless generator out-scores
meaningful text on every axis: word-order information for a block drift-null is
$\Delta I = 0.57$ vs $0.36$ for natural Latin, and the morphology network for a
meaningless abjad is $0.89$ vs $0.87$ for a constructed language---with the manuscript
sitting \emph{below both} endpoints ($\Delta I = 0.31$, morphology $0.80$). Every
VLM-computable statistic we tried is a structure detector, not a meaning detector.
\emph{The manuscript is maximally structured on every axis we can measure, yet no axis
separates meaning.}

\textbf{No encoding family is distinguished \grade{C}.} Under equal, held-out tuning
with de-collinearised metrics, no generative family (cipher, self-citation,
constructed language, abbreviation, abjad, and compositions thereof) is robustly
closest to the manuscript; a whitened (Mahalanobis) re-analysis agrees but is itself
regularisation-dependent (covariance condition number $\approx 1.0\times10^{4}$),
which only reinforces that the encoding ``bracket'' is a descriptive ordering, not
evidence for any family. \S4.6 sharpens this: while no family is \emph{selected}, one
broad class---cipher of real prose---is \emph{excluded}.

\subsection{A candidate positive, resolved to unresolved: the root$\leftrightarrow$leaf bundle}
The one associational signal that survived early scrutiny was a cross-organ visual
regularity: a plant's root colouring co-varying with its leaf arrangement (Cram\'er's
$V=0.40$). Its history is a cautionary tale in miniature. A first re-annotation model
failed to reproduce it (``single-model artifact''); a third model reproduced it and it
survived stratification by scribal hand and dialect and a palette-style control
(within-stratum permutation $p=0.003$/$0.014$); we then added a genuinely
out-of-lineage rater (a non-Anthropic frontier model whose root labels agree
$0.86$--$0.91$ with the others), and it did \emph{not} reproduce the association---no
cross-rater pairing survives. Crucially, the reproduce/not-reproduce split does not
track vendor lineage, and the leaf feature is noisy for every rater (pairwise
agreement $\approx 0.45$). On the high-confidence consensus subset (raters agreeing on
both organs) only $n=74$ pages remain, with minimum detectable effect $\phi\approx
0.33$---underpowered for the $\sim 0.28$ effect, and where labels are reliable the
association is $\approx$ nil ($V=0.19$, $p=0.63$). \textbf{The honest terminal status
is unresolved: the feature is too noisy for model annotation to adjudicate; a
pre-registered human panel is the only decisive test.} We record the whole arc,
including its flip-flops, rather than report whichever model was added last.

\subsection{Mid-level structure: where the structure lives \grade{Grade C}}
Having shown that magnitude-of-structure statistics cannot reach meaning, we built the
\emph{mid-level} layers between structure and semantics---collocation, word-classes,
morphology---each null-corrected (\S3) and stratified by Currier A/B.

\textbf{No natural-language surface function/content organisation \grade{C}.} Real
languages show a content$>$function collocational gap: content words have specific
collocates (peaked neighbour distributions) while frequent function words are flat.
Null-corrected against an order-shuffle baseline, this gap is strongly present in real
controls (Latin $z=19.1$, German $z=8.5$) but \emph{absent} in the manuscript
($z=-1.3$ for Currier~A, $-4.8$ for~B): its content-band words carry only near-chance
collocational selectivity, and its most-frequent words are, if anything, the \emph{more}
collocational---template-like local repeats rather than flat function words. The result
is robust across function/content band-cutoff choices.

\textbf{Weak distributional word-class structure \grade{C}.} Inducing word classes by
clustering context vectors and measuring adjacent-class transition information
\citep{brown1992class}, again null-corrected, real languages are strongly
class-structured ($z\approx14.8$) while the manuscript is only $\approx\!0.13$--$0.19\times$
that level in both dialects---weak part-of-speech organisation, robust across the number
of classes and context-vocabulary size.

\textbf{The two dialects do not differ in mid-level grammar (once content is
controlled) \grade{C}.} A global A-vs-B contrast suggested Currier~B carries more
word-class structure than~A; but Currier A/B is confounded with section (A dominates the
herbal, B the biological/recipe quires). The herbal is the only section containing both
dialects, giving a content-controlled comparison: there the apparent difference
\emph{reverses} (word-class $z$: global $B-A=+1.79$; within-herbal $B-A=-1.24$). So the
A/B mid-level difference is a section/content effect, not a dialect property---the two
systems' established difference is lexical, not grammatical (this within-herbal contrast
is itself underpowered, Herbal-B $\approx3.3$k tokens). \emph{Scope (L7): these are
surface-distributional results; a verbose/abbreviatory cipher or a template-driven
generator would depress surface word-syntax while leaving character and morphology
structure intact, so they do not prove the absence of an underlying grammar.}

\subsection{The cipher-of-real-prose class is excluded \grade{Grade B}}
The mid-level syntax measures (\S4.5) are not merely descriptive: they are a
cryptanalytic discriminator, because they behave differently under enciphering than
under generation. We assembled a \emph{joint signature}---character entropy $h_2$,
word-order information $\Delta I$, edit-distance-1 morphology, Zipf slope, and the two
null-corrected mid-level $z$-scores---for the manuscript and for candidate mechanisms
applied to real Latin, and asked which candidate matches the manuscript on
\emph{every} axis at once.

\textbf{Word-order-preserving ciphers keep the source language's strong syntax
\grade{B}.} A 1:1 substitution, a vowel-dropping abjad, and a light nomenclator applied
to Latin all inherit its strong surface syntax: on the two mid-level axes they sit at
function/content $z=13.8$/$21.0$/$9.8$ and word-class $z=11.3$/$13.0$ (nomenclator
excepted), while the manuscript is weak on both ($z=-1.2$/$1.9$ for Currier~A,
$-4.7$/$2.6$ for~B). The separation is roughly ten standard deviations, and the two
axes fail independently, so the exclusion does not hinge on a threshold. This closes,
on the \emph{joint} signature, the abjad/abbreviation class that \S4.2 had revived on
morphology alone.

\textbf{The exclusion is language-universal \grade{B}.} A refutation pass objected
that the mid-level measures had been calibrated only on Latin. Re-running them on
typologically diverse controls, \emph{no} natural language is weak: Romance (Latin
$z=20.0$/$14.9$, Italian $8.2$/$11.4$), Germanic (German $8.6$/$14.1$), and---decisively
for the abjad hypothesis---Semitic consonantal (Hebrew, a native abjad, $9.7$/$4.1$)
all sit far above the manuscript. An abjad of a real language therefore keeps the
strong surface syntax the manuscript lacks; the exclusion is not a Latin artifact.

\textbf{Transposition cannot rescue the class \grade{B}.} The one mechanism that
\emph{does} produce weak surface syntax is a transposition (order-scrambling) cipher
(function/content $z=2.2$, word-class $z=1.1$)---but a transposition destroys word-order
information, and the manuscript retains it ($\Delta I=0.16$/$0.20$, above the shuffle
floor $\approx0.01$). A minimal closure test makes the tension explicit and structural:
a deterministic-verbose transform of Latin lowers entropy to the manuscript band
($h_2=2.30$) while \emph{keeping} word order (thus $\Delta I=0.39$ and strong syntax
$z=20.0$); adding transposition forces weak syntax ($z=0.83$) but \emph{collapses}
$\Delta I$ to $0.01$. Retained-$\Delta I$ and weak word-syntax are mutually exclusive
under any (character-transform~$\times$~transposition) of real prose, yet the manuscript
has both. No candidate matches the full signature. \textbf{The entire
cipher-of-real-prose class is excluded on the joint signature.} The resolution, from the
established block/section structure of the manuscript's $\Delta I$ (\S4.1), is that its
retained word-order information is \emph{positional/template} structure rather than
linguistic word order: the evidence points to a template-driven / positional generative
system, not an enciphering of real prose. \emph{This is a statistical class-exclusion;
it makes no decipherment or meaning claim (L7), and the one candidate that matched the
manuscript's weak syntax---the H3 self-citation generator---is Voynich-tuned by
construction and so is not counted as independent positive evidence for any specific
generator.}

\subsection{The favoured generative class, characterised and constrained \grade{Grade C}}
Having excluded the cipher-of-real-prose class and having pointed to template/positional
generation, we tested that favoured class directly---can such a generator, \emph{not}
tuned to the manuscript, reproduce the \emph{full} eight-axis signature? The answer,
after a refutation pass overturned a first-pass positive, is an informative
\emph{negative} that sharpens the constraint.

\textbf{A context-free positional generator is insufficient.} We built a three-ingredient
generator---a positional character grammar (disjoint small glyph inventories per slot), a
block-theme wrapper, and context-free slot-filling---whose parameters were swept over an
a-priori grid rather than fitted. It reproduces the manuscript's character entropy
($h_2=2.14$), block-scale $\Delta I$ ($0.08$), and (via block contrast) its
weak-but-positive word-class structure, but across a $64$-point a-priori grid it does not
\emph{simultaneously} match the manuscript's morphology-network connectivity
(edit-distance-1 main component $\approx 0.75$; the generator runs high, $\approx
0.97$--$1.0$), its lexical reuse (type-token ratio $\approx 0.22$; generator $\approx
0.59$), or its frequency slope. These are not proven unreachable---connectivity and slope
move toward band at the grid's edge---but they are \emph{coupled}: the branching that
lowers connectivity raises entropy out of band, and the concentration that lowers the
type-token ratio does likewise, so the context-free ``bag of slots'' cannot place them
in-band together. Two of the eight axes carry little independent weight here: the
function/content and word-class $z$-scores are scored against two-point Currier~A/B ranges
(not bootstrap intervals), and a control shows the manuscript's weak-positive word-class
$z$ is reproduced by real Latin word \emph{types} sampled context-free under the same
block wrapper ($z_{fc}=-1.4$, $z_{wc}=2.5$)---so that ``positive'' signal is sectional
vocabulary drift, not a grammatical feature a generator must earn, and we do not lean on
it. \emph{Process note (a self-correction on the record):} a first-pass verdict had
graded this generator a ``class sufficiency'' at grade~B; the refutation pass showed its
constants had been grid-selected to hit the manuscript's bands (a fitted point, not an
a-priori draw) and that its weak-syntax test used a one-sided threshold a full order
shuffle also passes---and the corrected, band-honest analysis turned the apparent
positive into this negative.

\textbf{Adding word reuse helps but hits a Pareto tension.} The three missed axes are all
frequency-concentration failures, so we added a word-reuse (copy-from-history) mechanism
and swept it a-priori ($104$ configurations, including global preferential attachment).
Reuse individually rescues every missed axis---connectivity in-band from copy-rate
$\rho\geq 0.6$, reuse from $\rho\geq 0.4$, frequency slope from $\rho\geq 0.8$---and
global preferential attachment additionally \emph{restores} the manuscript's weak-positive
word-class structure ($z_{wc}$ from $-1.0$ up into band, though as just noted that axis is
soft). But no configuration satisfies even the whole frequency group at once, let alone
jointly with the entropy/$\Delta I$ group (the grid's ceiling is four of eight axes): the
copy rate that concentrates frequency simultaneously deflates the character entropy and
the block-scale $\Delta I$. So token-level copying does not, at the swept frequency
exponent and block length, concentrate frequency without spending entropy and~$\Delta I$.

\textbf{Type-level concentration resolves that trade-off but leaves a residual coupling.}
The natural fix is to concentrate frequency at the \emph{type} level---a genuinely small,
skewed lexicon of positional-grammar words, sampled context-free---rather than by copying
tokens. Swept a-priori ($144$ configurations over lexicon size, branching, frequency
exponent, and block contrast), this \emph{does} achieve what token reuse could not: the
type-token ratio now sits in band \emph{jointly} with the character entropy, dissolving
the entropy-versus-reuse tension. Yet the full signature is still not reached (ceiling
again four of eight): the obstruction migrates to \emph{morphological connectivity}---
matching the manuscript's edit-distance-1 connectivity ($\approx 0.75$) forces a
lexicon/branching regime that is out of band on entropy, reuse, and frequency slope---
together with a block-contrast trade-off (retained $\Delta I$ favours weak block contrast
while a positive word-class $z$ favours strong contrast). Across the three families we
sweep---context-free positional, positional-plus-token-reuse, and positional-plus-small-
lexicon---none reproduces the manuscript's full eight-axis signature over the swept ranges;
its summary statistics are mutually coupled in a way these mechanisms do not capture. We
state this as a constraint on those families, not as a proof that no generative process
can match: the sweeps fix word length and slot count, use a single random seed without
generator-side resampling, and leave untested corners (steeper frequency laws crossed with
reuse, a type lexicon decoupled from the slot grammar) that are the named next steps.
(Grade C; no sufficiency and no identification are claimed---L7.)

\section{Discussion}
Two substantive conclusions and one methodological one. Substantively: (i) the
manuscript is a genuine, richly structured, two-system formal script whose morphology
network is reachable only by a length-preserving script over an already-structured
inventory---which had revived the abjad/abbreviation class and disfavoured verbose
ciphers, until the joint-signature test (\S4.6) excluded the broader
cipher-of-real-prose class of which it is part; (ii) whether that structure carries
\emph{meaning} is underdetermined, and we show \emph{why} it is hard: the statistics
that quantify structure (word-order information, character entropy, morphological
density) do not discriminate meaning, because structured-meaningless processes reproduce
or exceed them. This reframes the central question from ``what does it say'' to ``how far
along each interpretable dimension does it sit,'' and marks the honest boundary at which
purely distributional methods stop. (iii)~The mid-level probes (\S4.5) locate
\emph{where} the structure lives: strongly at the character (entropy anomaly) and
morphology (edit-distance-1 network) levels, but \emph{weakly at the word level}---no
natural-language function/content collocation, weak word-class organisation. The
cryptanalytic reading of that profile (\S4.6) is the program's sharpest negative to
date: a system that is highly regular below the word, retains block-scale positional
information, yet is syntactically thin above the word, cannot be produced by any cipher
of real prose---order-preserving ciphers keep the plaintext's strong syntax, and
transposition ciphers destroy the retained positional information; only a template-driven
or positional \emph{generative} process reconciles all three properties. Yet that
favoured generative account is itself incomplete (\S4.7): across the three families we
sweep---context-free positional, positional-plus-token-reuse, and positional-plus-small-
lexicon---none reproduces the manuscript's morphology connectivity, lexical reuse, and
frequency law \emph{jointly} with its entropy and $\Delta I$; the axes trade off against
one another, each mechanism dissolving the previous blocker and exposing a new one (token
reuse trades frequency against entropy; type-level concentration then trades morphological
connectivity against the rest). The constraint envelope has thus tightened from both
sides: no cipher of real prose fits, and no simple generative model \emph{we tested} fits
either over the swept ranges, so the manuscript sits in a narrow region that is easy to
describe axis-by-axis but that no tested mechanism occupies all at once---a coupling we
report as a constraint on these families rather than an impossibility for all. That the two Currier systems share this mid-level profile (their difference
being lexical, not grammatical) further constrains ``two languages'' readings toward ``two
registers/vocabularies of one system.''

Methodologically, the architecture is the result. The clean-context refutation pass
overturned, before publication, several of the program's own most attractive
conclusions: a ``meaning certificate'' read of the word-order statistic; a
``constructed-language best fit''; a ``needs constructed morphology'' claim (refuted by
the abjad control the reviewer demanded); a ``whitening confirms'' claim (withdrawn
once the covariance was shown ill-conditioned); a set of false-positive anchors caught
only by a mandatory null control; a positive root$\leftrightarrow$leaf verdict, first
over-claimed and then over-killed, corrected to unresolved; an apparent Currier
A-vs-B grammatical difference that a dedicated content-controlled study overturned as a
section confound; a first-pass ``the manuscript is favoured as a
generation process'' read of the joint-signature test, rejected as circular (its only
match was a Voynich-tuned generator) and narrowed to the robust negative---after which
the refutation's own demanded control (typologically diverse languages) \emph{upgraded}
that negative from Latin-specific to universal; and, most recently, a ``the favoured
generative class is sufficient'' claim (grade~B) overturned when the refutation showed the
generator's constants had been \emph{grid-selected to hit the manuscript's own bands}---a
fitted point mislabelled a-priori, the very circularity flagged one iteration earlier---and
its weak-syntax test used a threshold a random shuffle also passes, so the corrected,
band-honest analysis reduced it to a precise negative. Several mid-level probes were themselves
refused for want of a clean null rather than reported as weak evidence. A pipeline that
declines to over-read a negative as readily as a positive, and that can overturn a
verdict asserted by its own code or its own prior iteration, is, we argue, the
transferable contribution to undeciphered-corpus research.

\section{Limitations}
Visual features are model-annotated and noisy (leaf-arrangement inter-rater agreement
$\approx 0.45$), which caps power on any imagery-based test; several conclusions rest
on a single manuscript-length corpus and are correspondingly power-limited; the extant
text is itself incomplete ($\approx\!12\%$ of the foliated range is lost and the
vocabulary is non-saturating, so the missing folios likely held unseen types), which
bounds every lexical and anchor statistic below; all vision raters to date share
broadly similar training lineages, so ``independence'' is cross-vendor, not absolute;
the cipher-of-real-prose exclusion (\S4.6) is computed over constructions of a Latin
plaintext with a diverse-language control on the mid-level axes, not over every possible
plaintext language or every exotic cipher; the generative-incompleteness result (\S4.7) is
over three families (context-free positional, token-reuse, small-lexicon) swept with
fixed word length and slot count, a single random seed, and no generator-side resampling,
and two of its eight axes (the function/content and word-class $z$-scores) are scored
against two-point dialect ranges rather than confidence intervals and are confounded with
sectional vocabulary drift; so it constrains those families over those ranges rather than
proving that \emph{no} generative process can match, and its tight single-seed in/out
calls invite multi-seed replication; and text results are primarily EVA-based,
with v101 as a sensitivity layer rather than a full replication. Grades reflect these
limits.

\section{Future Work}
The decisive next test for the root$\leftrightarrow$leaf question is a pre-registered
independent \emph{human} panel on the high-confidence consensus subset, with a power
analysis reported first; more models cannot settle a noise-limited question. The
generative-account result (\S4.7) names its own next steps. Type-level concentration
already dissolved the entropy-versus-reuse tension but left morphological connectivity as
the residual obstruction, so the decisive tests are now (i)~multi-seed replication with
generator-side resampling, to convert the tight single-seed in/out calls into
confidence-interval overlaps; (ii)~the untested corners the present sweeps extrapolate
over---branching below the grid floor, steeper frequency laws crossed with reuse, and a
type lexicon \emph{decoupled} from the slot grammar so that connectivity can be tuned
independently of entropy; and (iii)~a morphology model whose edit-distance connectivity is
not rigidly coupled to word length. Only if these too leave the axes mutually incompatible
would the headline strengthen toward ``no tested generative family reproduces the joint
signature.'' The mid-level results additionally
invite a larger content-matched A-vs-B sample (the within-herbal contrast is
underpowered) to firm up the ``no grammatical dialect difference'' finding, and a
long-range/hierarchical dependency probe to complete the mid-level layer. None of these
targets translation; each targets the grammar of the system, which is what the evidence
can bear.

\section*{Reproducibility}
All statistics are produced by deterministic, versioned code (fixed seeds) writing
machine-readable JSON to \texttt{results/}; every reported number records its
producing script, git commit, dataset version, and parameters. Source and
data-processing code accompany this preprint.
